_what: Clinical weight per gene for the cb++ score. EDIT THIS -- it is a domain judgment, not a measurement, and it is deliberately in its own file so it can be argued with without touching code.
_scale: 1.00 = a gene whose disruption causes a named, common, clinically managed coagulopathy. 0.40 = coagulation-adjacent, real but seldom the thing a haematologist is looking for.
_note: OAS1 and GSDMB are immune genes carried over from 13-intronhunt. They are 0 so they never enter cb++, but they stay in the browser as an out-of-domain comparison set.

_rationale.1.00: F8/F9 haemophilia A and B; VWF von Willebrand disease -- the three commonest inherited bleeding disorders. F5 and F2 carry the two commonest inherited thrombophilias (Factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A). SERPINC1/PROC/PROS1 are the classical severe thrombophilias.
_rationale.0.85: Named rare factor deficiencies that are diagnosed and treated. ADAMTS13 is TTP. VKORC1 is here for pharmacogenomic reach rather than deficiency -- it is the principal warfarin dosing locus, so a regulatory variant has direct prescribing relevance.
_rationale.0.70: Real coagulation biology with a smaller or more variable clinical footprint.
_rationale.0.55: Coagulation-adjacent: initiation, fibrinolysis, secretion chaperones. A finding here needs more argument.
_rationale.0.40: Contact activation. FXII and prekallikrein deficiency prolong aPTT without causing bleeding, which is exactly the 'no human relevance' objection this score exists to avoid.
